methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + similar-valuation-tier peers in AI & Software. Range: $29.0B - $312.5B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in AI & Compute

data.narrative:
Waymo, a pre-IPO autonomous vehicle software company, is evaluated against a peer set of 9 AI & Software companies: one public (Palantir, trading at $312.5B) and eight private firms including Figure AI ($39.0B), Scale AI ($29.0B), Reflection AI, and Applied Intuition.

The peer-median method applies directly to Waymo's stage and sector positioning. The three primary comparables—Palantir, Figure AI, and Scale AI—anchor a median valuation of $39.0B, with a documented range spanning $29.0B to $312.5B. This wide dispersion reflects heterogeneity in the AI & Software peer set, particularly the Palantir outlier at $312.5B relative to the tighter clustering of Scale AI and Figure AI. The peer-median approach yields an implied valuation of $39.0B.

The triangulation analysis supports a range of $33.1B to $44.9B (median $39.0B), though this reflects single-method support and thus carries material uncertainty. Key vulnerabilities include: limited methodological diversity (one applicable approach), substantial valuation scatter across the peer universe (10x spread between lowest and highest), and the absence of revenue, profitability, or growth metrics to calibrate relative positioning within the range. Waymo's current $126B valuation sits materially above the peer-derived range, suggesting either: meaningful performance differentials not captured by peer comparables, significant private-market froth, or valuation disconnects requiring reconciliation through forward-looking financial metrics not present in this dataset.
